figures.title: The decision-grade evaluation circuit
figures.desc: A five-stage circuit moves from a bounded claim through construct mapping, risk-targeted coverage, an independent decision set, and four exact verdicts with a reject-to-new-version return.
figures.caption: At VERDICT: ACCEPT BOUNDED stops; REJECT returns to a new version and fresh holdout; EVAL INVALID and INCONCLUSIVE stop the claim until evidence is repaired.
figures.transcript: First, bound the exact claim and decision use. Second, map the construct into observable dimensions and excluded proxies. Third, cover ordinary and high-risk operating conditions with open development cases. Fourth, freeze the harness, charter, scorer, and invalidation rules before running the independent decision set. Fifth, issue ACCEPT BOUNDED, REJECT, EVAL INVALID, or INCONCLUSIVE. A rejected harness may be improved using the now-exposed case, but the next acceptance circuit requires a fresh independent decision set.

items.label: 4 VERDICTS
items.detail: ACCEPT BOUNDED / REJECT / EVAL INVALID / INCONCLUSIVE

figures.title: Coverage before the independent decision set
figures.desc: Four linked zones distinguish the construct map, open development cases, independent decision cases, and the one-way decision gate.
figures.caption: Inspect what may feed tuning and what must remain outside it until the declared gate.
figures.transcript: The construct map defines dimensions, operating conditions, high-risk pressures, excluded qualities, and critical gates. The open set covers those cells and may feed repeated tuning. The independent decision set covers named cells too, but its content, expected results, and scoring rationale remain unavailable to harness authors and their systems. At the declared gate, the frozen harness runs once and the fixed rule controls the verdict. After evaluation, decision cases become development evidence and cannot approve the next version.

figures.title: Route a bad result before diagnosing the harness
figures.desc: A diagnostic table separates a valid harness failure from construct misses, holdout leakage, and scorer ambiguity, with a different next move for each.
figures.caption: Find the first broken evidence condition; only a valid case and intact gate support a harness verdict.
figures.transcript: When a valid in-construct case reaches an intact sealed gate and violates a frozen critical rule, the result is a harness failure and the acceptance claim is rejected. When the case misses the construct or a coverage cell has no defensible relation to the intended use, the eval is invalid and the map or case must be repaired. When case content, expected labels, or scoring rationale reached the tuning path, the holdout is void and must be replaced. When scorers cannot apply the frozen rubric consistently, the result is inconclusive until the rubric is clarified prospectively and fresh evidence is collected.
